headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces, but documentation-only evidence limits certainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, and agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP channels. There is no documented bridge for A’s content to reach B as instructions, so prompt injection is not plausible in this pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator manually copies A’s text into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF B is reconfigured to ingest files or clipboard content, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from copy-paste workflows.
Do not route A’s repository text into B as system or developer messages.
Verify B remains without clipboard/stdin/file ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network egress none; B also has no filesystem read, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible leakage path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or secrets, leakage analysis must be revisited.
IF a shared workspace is added, data flow assumptions change.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces.
Do not mount sensitive directories into either agent.
Confirm B stays read_filesystem=false and network_egress=none.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if file access is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network permissions documented, and B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so capability conflict is effectively blocked.
conditions: IF A is later granted write or network capabilities, overlap may emerge.
IF B gains filesystem or git write access, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep B’s write and git permissions disabled.
Avoid placing A behind an orchestrator that grants hidden write access.
Review any future capability changes before co-running.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a documentation-only content writer with no stdin/stdout or API calls, so it cannot automatically act on A’s outputs. A is a course repository, not an action-taking agent. Any cascade would require manual human transfer, making the pathway unusual and the blast radius small.
conditions: IF a human manually pastes A-generated text into B as authoritative source material, cascading error becomes possible.
IF B is connected to an external publishing pipeline, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before B uses A-derived content.
Label A outputs as untrusted reference material.
Keep B disconnected from publishing or automation.
requires-engineering: add citation checks if A feeds B in future.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either agent, and both profiles show docs-only, open-source, non-runnable artifacts with no secrets, OAuth scopes, or residency-sensitive processing. The pair does not present a documented compliance mismatch.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention policies are added later, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency if either profile changes.
Recheck compliance before any deployment change.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if sensitive data is introduced.
